title: Singleton mass differences sum to zero
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite discrete measurable space, and let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be probability measures on $\Omega$. Then the singleton mass differences sum to zero:
\[
\sum_{\omega \in \Omega} \bigl(\mu(\{\omega\}) - \nu(\{\omega\})\bigr) = 0.
\]
hypotheses_covered: Ω is a finite discrete measurable space
μ is a probability measure on Ω
ν is a probability measure on Ω
replaced:
On a finite measurable space, the singleton mass differences sum to zero:
$\sum_{\omega : \Omega} (\mu(\{\omega\}) - \nu(\{\omega\})) = 0$.
